title: Machine learning predicts vomiting in children admitted for cancer or stem cell transplant
summary: Models were trained on electronic health record data from 7,408 paediatric oncology and hematopoietic cell transplant admissions; the best, a LightGBM model with 2,859 features trained on all inpatients, reached an AUROC of 0.730 (95% CI 0.694 to 0.765). In a prospective silent trial of 340 admissions the AUROC was 0.716 (95% CI 0.649 to 0.784). Discrimination is moderate and the model was not deployed, so benefit for vomiting control is untested.
ai_technology: LightGBM model (also tested: L2 logistic regression, XGBoost) on electronic health record data

evidence.tested: Prospective silent trial of 340 admissions: AUROC 0.716.
evidence.unknown: Not deployed; effect on vomiting control unknown; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A gradient boosting model predicted vomiting risk within 96 hours from routine record data.
